provider: Nakala (Huma-Num, France) - no formal size limit, but a HumanID gate and a conversation with the team

free_tier.stated: 'There is no formal limitation on the size of data deposited'; above ~10 GB per file you must contact the Nakala team first. Private pre-publication space is capped far lower (9,999 items or 100 GB), so the large-volume path is publish-as-you-go.
free_tier.notes: Headline offer; binding constraint specified in limits.

per_object_cap.notes: extracted from the quota or limits prose

retention.stated: No retention statement documented in published terms; absence is not an unlimited claim.
retention.notes: extraction found no retention clause; the seed's limits text may still state one, see extras.limits_verbatim

egress.terms: Free public HTTPS with a DOI per deposit; no egress metering published.

tooling: Nakala REST API plus nakalot (multipart batch uploader driven by a CSV/XLS manifest); OAI-PMH.
chaining: Per deposit, unlimited deposits - but the gate is identity, not bytes.
limits_note: Account path is HumanID -> request Nakala access -> 'Discuss the scientific and technical project associated with the deposit with HumaNum's team'. Research data only, must be documented to a metadata schema, licence from a closed list, ORCID checked on authors. Published deposits cannot be deleted unilaterally.
reliability_note: MESR-funded national infrastructure, data preserved at CINES after audit; ~100 TB of storage on the ISIDORE/Nakala stack. French research context in practice.

extras.agent_focus: Bulk data programmes that pay for your storage. Two halves: (1) institutional/gov repositories and cloud open-data sponsorships, judged as free byte pools; (2) research grants that could fund storage for an unaffiliated individual. Revisited AWS ODS, Google Cloud public datasets, Source Cooperative. Central question for each: what is the unit of quota (account / record / dataset / collection / project), because that unit is the multiplier.

binding_note: the quota is real and unreachable: identity is the binding constraint, and it is not one of the six limits kinds
